keyframe_review.note: 1.22 M km2 for 1863-1864 against the infobox 1.33 M km2 (undated; ratio 0.92). The page says the country 'comprised the present-day nations of Colombia and Panama and parts of northwestern Brazil'; Cliopatria's outline holds Panama and the Colombian claim in the Peruvian Amazon, not the Brazilian part. The nine sovereign states (Antioquia, Bolívar, Boyacá, Cauca, Cundinamarca, Magdalena, Panamá, Santander, Tolima) are all inside. The page says Panamá 'joined the union on May 8, 1863'. Constitution promulgated 8 May 1863, so the first four months of the Cliopatria year belong to the Granadine Confederation.
Same outline for 1865; the page records no territorial change under the federal constitution. The Federal District of Bogotá was suppressed on 11 May 1864.

correction.text: the same 1.22 M km2 outline that Cliopatria draws under 'Republic of Colombia' from 1866, held to the end of the United States of Colombia in 1886

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, confidence 2: the page has the United States of Colombia last until 1886 ('Disestablished: 1886'; the 1886 constitution 'abolished the United States of Colombia and created the Republic of Colombia'), but Cliopatria renames the state in 1866. The 1866-1885 outline is identical to the 1863-1865 one, so the republic-of-colombia dossier should begin its life in 1886 and treat Cliopatria's 1866-1885 years as these. The page records no territorial change in the period.

region.text: the whole country as a federation of nine sovereign states

ledger.note: 8 May 1863: the Rionegro Constitution makes the Granadine Confederation the United States of Colombia. 'On 3 February 1863, Congress approved the name United States of Colombia for the country. On 8 May, the Constitución de Rionegro was promulgated', creating a federal system of nine sovereign states with a two-year presidency; Mosquera 'was chosen to be the first president' on 12 May.

1886: Núñez's constitution abolishes the United States of Colombia. 'during 1886 the Colombian Conservative Party led by President Rafael Núñez proclaimed a new constitution of a unitary and centralist character' that 'abolished the United States of Colombia and created the Republic of Colombia'; the infobox ends the state in 1886 (José María Campo Serrano, last president).

certainty.note: The page gives no boundary treaty; the Amazon frontiers with Peru, Brazil and Ecuador were claims, and the Panama–Costa Rica line was not fixed.

notes: Cliopatria's United States of Colombia row stops after 1865 and its 'Republic of Colombia' row (slug republic-of-colombia, written by another part) runs 1866-2024 on the same outline, but the page keeps the United States of Colombia to 1886: this dossier therefore carries a new keyframe 1866-1886 and ends in 1886; republic-of-colombia should start in 1886 and mark its 1866-1885 shapes as belonging to this state. No wars were researched for 1863-1886 within the page budget (the page opened names none; the civil wars of the 1870s and 1880s need their own pages), so the wars list is empty; a gap-filler should open the page on the 1876 and 1884-85 civil wars. The 1863 year is shared with granadine-confederation (8 May 1863). The page puts Mosquera's first presidency at 1863-1864 and says the name 'United States of Colombia' was first used by Mosquera in November 1861. The Federal District of Bogotá (23 July 1861 – 11 May 1864) is an internal subdivision and moves no border. Panamá's 1855 creation and its 1903 secession are outside this dossier except as the page mentions them. No dated border event is recorded on the page in 1863-1886, so none is in the ledger.
